This temporary post exercises the main parts of the blog. It can be deleted after the design has been checked.

## Typography

Body text supports **bold**, *emphasis*, ~~strikethrough~~, and `inline code`.

> Good tools should make the common path easy and the unusual path possible.

### Lists

1. Write Markdown in `content/blog/`.
2. Build the site.
3. Publish by setting `draft: false`.

- [x] Semantic Markdown
- [x] On-demand Tree-sitter highlighting
- [x] Rust viewer controls, with a small JavaScript grammar-loader bridge

## Rust highlighting

Code is readable immediately. The browser loads the requested Tree-sitter grammar on demand, then reuses it across blocks and pages.

```rust title="sequence.rs" {9-14}
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
struct Sequence<'a> {
    id: &'a str,
    bases: &'a [u8],
}

impl Sequence<'_> {
    fn gc_fraction(&self) -> f64 {
        let gc = self
            .bases
            .iter()
            .filter(|base| matches!(base, b'G' | b'C'))
            .count();

        gc as f64 / self.bases.len() as f64
    }
}
```

## Other languages

Languages do not need a Cargo feature or an application rebuild to become available.

```python title="sequence.py"
def gc_fraction(sequence):
    bases = sequence.upper()
    return sum(base in "GC" for base in bases) / len(bases)
```

```typescript title="sequence.ts"
const bases: string = "ACGT";
console.log(bases.length);
```

```nix title="shell.nix"
{ pkgs }:
pkgs.mkShell { packages = [ pkgs.rustc ]; }
```

Nested code keeps its surrounding Markdown structure and receives the same highlighting:

> A small Python example:
>
> ```python
> print("<hello> & goodbye")
> ```
>
> The code belongs to this quotation.

## Tables

| Feature | Implementation | Browser cost |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| Markdown | `pulldown-cmark` | None |
| Syntax highlighting | Tree-sitter via Arborium | On-demand WASM grammar |
| Post catalog | Generated by `build.rs` | Static data |
